record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: What formal privacy guarantees can be proved for split learning, including guarantees that account for the information leaked by communicated activations or smashed data from clients to the server?

evidence.quote: Overall, much of the discussion in Section 4 is relevant here as well, and analysis providing formal privacy guarantees speciﬁcally for split learning is still an open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Split learning is a distributed machine learning protocol in which a neural network f = f_server ∘ f_client is partitioned at a designated "cut layer" between a client and a server. The client holds private input data x (and possibly labels y) and computes the forward pass up to the cut layer, transmitting the intermediate activations a = f_client(x; θ_client) (the "smashed data") to the server. The server completes the forward pass, computes the loss, and sends gradients back through the cut layer so the client can update θ_client. Training and/or inference proceeds over many rounds, during which the server observes the sequence of smashed activations (and, in training, receives gradients on them) for every client input.

Problem. Develop a rigorous privacy analysis of split learning. Specifically:

1. Define a precise threat model for split learning that specifies (a) the adversary's role (honest-but-curious or malicious server, colluding clients, or external eavesdroppers), (b) the adversary's auxiliary knowledge (architecture, parameters, public data distribution), and (c) the observable transcript, including the smashed activations a_t = f_client(x_t; θ_client^{(t)}) sent from clients across all training and inference rounds, together with any gradient signals returned to the client.

2. Under this threat model, prove formal privacy guarantees for the client's raw inputs (and labels, where relevant) against the server. The guarantees should be expressible in a standard cryptographic or statistical privacy framework — for example, (ε, δ)-differential privacy, Rényi differential privacy, mutual-information bounds I(x ; transcript) ≤ β, or simulation-based / indistinguishability guarantees — and must explicitly account for the information leaked by the communicated activations (smashed data) and any associated gradients, not merely the leakage from the final trained model.

3. Quantify the privacy/utility tradeoff: state and prove how the privacy parameters depend on the choice of cut layer, the dimensionality and statistics of the smashed data, the number of communication rounds, and any randomization mechanism (e.g. additive noise, clipping, or cryptographic protocol) applied to the activations, and exhibit matching upper and lower bounds whenever possible.

Provide such a formal privacy guarantee, or prove an impossibility result showing that no nontrivial guarantee of the specified form can hold for vanilla split learning.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has provided partial formal privacy analyses of split learning under specific threat models: information-theoretic lower bounds on reconstruction error via Fisher-approximated Shannon information (2025), differentially private split learning schemes with accuracy/privacy tradeoffs, and cryptographic constructions using Function Secret Sharing that provably eliminate activation leakage. However, a comprehensive and tight formal privacy framework that quantifies leakage from smashed data across general split-learning protocols and architectures remains an active research area, with continuing demonstrations of new reconstruction attacks against vanilla split learning.

status_evidence.title: Quantifying Privacy Leakage in Split Inference via Fisher-Approximated Shannon Information Analysis
status_evidence.snippet: formalize privacy leakage against DRAs within an information-theoretic framework and derive both average-case and worst-case lower bounds on adversary reconstruction error
status_evidence.claim: Provides formal information-theoretic privacy guarantees for split inference via a new FSInfo metric.

status_evidence.title: InfoDecom: Decomposing Information for Defending Against Privacy Leakage in Split Inference
status_evidence.snippet: achieves theoretical privacy guarantees against DRAs in shallow-client split inference systems
status_evidence.claim: Provides theoretically guaranteed privacy via calibrated noise after information decomposition.

status_evidence.title: Enhancing Accuracy-Privacy Trade-off in Differentially Private Split Learning
status_evidence.snippet: differentially private split learning ... accuracy-privacy trade-off
status_evidence.claim: Differential privacy mechanisms applied to split learning provide formal (ε,δ)-DP guarantees.

status_evidence.title: Oops!… They Stole it Again: Attacks on Split Learning
status_evidence.claim: New reconstruction attacks against split learning continue to be demonstrated, indicating no general formal guarantee is in place for vanilla split learning.
